div.div: A low SM issue rate is not free room: about half the kernel time already fills an SM on some resource, and multi-wave kernels would be expected to gain from more SMs (illustrative, theoretical)
Two different questions about the GPU and one SM (schematic gauges; per-SM limits of an Orin-class board)

div.b: warp-slot fill of the large GEMM kernels (fraction of slots, not of time)

div.div: 0.1–0.3 [gemm_warp_slot_fill]

div.b: kernel time in > 1 wave, per service

div.div: 0.35–0.7 [multiwave_share, illustrative]

Why a GEMM fills an SM with few warps (worked register limit). To fill all 48 warp slots a kernel may use at most about 40 registers per thread: 65 536 ÷ 48 = 1365.3 per warp, rounded down to a multiple of 256 = 1280, ÷ 32 threads = 40 (my estimate from `registers_per_sm`, `max_warps_per_sm`, `warp_size` and `register_alloc_unit_per_warp`). A GEMM kernel often uses far more, up to 255 per thread [max_registers_per_thread], so its SM is full by registers with only a few warps resident.
Waves (schematic): waves = ⌈blocks ÷ (SMs × blocks per SM)⌉. Below, one block per SM for clarity: a kernel with blocks for two full rounds and a partial third on the 16 SMs [sm_count_orin].
wave 1
wave 2
wave 3 (partial)

More SMs -> fewer waves: roughly in proportion for kernels with many waves; in steps, possibly none, for kernels with only a few waves, because the last wave rounds up; no gain where a kernel is limited by DRAM bandwidth, L2 or memory latency (not measured per kernel). An expectation, not a measurement.

Two corrections kept visible
• "A low issue rate means room for MPS": wrong. A register-bound GEMM fills its SMs with few warps, so issue is low while no other block fits.
• "More SMs mostly add idle SMs": wrong for multi-wave kernels.

What it means for MPS (hypothesis, page 05). In the rest of the kernel time (small grids, partial last waves, kernels below 90 % on every resource) kernels of two processes could overlap. During full kernels MPS mainly lets the other process's blocks start as SM resources free up, instead of after a whole time slice and a context switch.

Caveats. Fill numbers are theoretical, from launch configurations in solo traces; achieved occupancy, stall reasons and co-residency under MPS were not measured, nor why issue is low. Traces had limits (a different VLA model version; a replay-fed detector; an empty people-perception scene). The gauges on the left are a schematic.

Legend
green solid bar = share with SMs full; white bar, dashed green = warp-slot fill
blue bar = share in > 1 wave; blue squares = SMs busy in a wave
faint dotted bar = below the low end of a range
gauges: solid = value or range low end; dashed = range high end or GPU-active share
dashed vertical line = the "full" definition; purple dashed = a correction

Sources. Note B2. Occupancy and issue rate: ../../nvidia-gpu-anatomy/ (note 03); board limits: ../../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/. The "full" threshold is read from the source text of kernel_time_sms_full_share.
Illustrative (round teaching numbers that keep the shape of a finding; not measurements): sm_issue_full_stack, gpu_active_full_stack, gemm_warp_slot_fill, kernel_time_sms_full_share, multiwave_share.
Sibling (keys in a sibling public kit; paths relative to the kit folder): max_warps_per_sm = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json max_warps_per_sm; registers_per_sm = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json registers_per_sm; l1_shared_per_sm_orin_kb = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json l1_shared_per_sm.orin; sm_count_orin = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json sm_count.orin.
Public: max_blocks_per_sm_cc87 = https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/ (technical specifications per compute capability; occupancy); warp_size = https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/ (technical specifications per compute capability; occupancy); register_alloc_unit_per_warp = https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/ (technical specifications per compute capability; occupancy); max_registers_per_thread = https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/ (technical specifications per compute capability; occupancy).
